prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a ligand-controlled and mechanistically understood method for constructing aryl amines.

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B021 to B004, Buchwald and Hartwig. In round 1 I asked Somfai to separate what was discovered beyond the Pd-catalysed C-C precedent, and his answer is the one I needed: C-N coupling required a different mechanistic solution (amine binding, deprotonation, and a difficult C-N reductive elimination) and a new ligand toolbox that suppresses beta-hydride elimination and catalyst deactivation. Zou gave the same account independently. Judged by my own physicist's test, there is one underlying principle, ligand control over the elementary steps of a catalytic cycle, backed by quantitative mechanistic work and about thirty years of independent confirmation. The attribution is a clean pair and the citation can be explained in two sentences: a general way to make aryl amines, now used daily in medicinal and process chemistry, agrochemicals and materials. Round 1 left no majority, and B004 is the only candidate that nobody has called unworthy or immature and that carries no unresolved credit dispute.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize remains a real objection, and Aqvist, Chabes and Sparr weigh it more heavily than Somfai and Zou do. I regard it as an enabling precedent rather than a bar, but a reader of the citation may still see a new bond type for an honoured concept, and the mature, synthesis-centred character of the work looks conservative beside delivery chemistry. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor, and the citation must be worded as the general catalytic method so it is not open to a priority challenge. The expert reports should confirm that the stoichiometric tin chemistry was not general. The two-name configuration also leaves a slot unused, which I accept as better than an unsupported third name.

responses.point: Somfai argued that C-N coupling needed a different mechanism and ligand solution than the 2010 C-C prize, namely amine binding, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination, plus ligands that suppress beta-hydride elimination, and that B004 is used daily by bench chemists where the Lagrangian scheme is used mostly by specialists.
responses.response: This answers the question I put to him, and it changes my position. A different rate-limiting and selectivity problem, solved by a new ligand design principle, is a distinct discovery and not an extension by analogy. His point about breadth of adoption also weighs on B021: its reach runs largely through successor schemes and specialist use. I agree with his handling of Kosugi, with the precursor mentioned at most and the citation anchored to the general catalytic method. Where I still differ from him is the strength of the 2010 objection, which I think the committee should record as a risk and not wave away.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B040 as the largest real-world consequence, defends Cullis, MacLachlan and Anderson on the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid, and keeps B004 as first alternative while holding the 2010 prize against it.
responses.response: I share his reading of B040's impact and I keep it as my first alternative. The question I posed, who first demonstrated the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid principle for in vivo delivery, has not been settled in round 1. The supporters each concede it rests on recollection, and Chabes and Zou name Hope and Madden as essential. I cannot defend a citation that excludes contributors the committee itself regards as essential, so I cannot move B040 above a clean pair. If the reports establish a trio, I would reconsider. His point that Car-Parrinello has fewer single results traceable to it than a drug or vaccine is fair, and it is part of why I have left B021.

responses.point: Chabes considers B046 on the principle of induced proximity, accepts that no designed PROTAC is approved, and says the case must stand on mechanism, while he would not oppose Buchwald and Hartwig as a safe, mechanistically solid award.
responses.response: I think the case for B046 as one citation fails on his own terms. He says it has to stand on the chemistry and the mechanism, and the Handa cereblon mechanism and the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC concept are separate findings, with Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito outside any three-person cap. That is the credit problem I put to Aili and that Brzezinski and Somfai also raise. I welcome his statement that the overlap with 2010 is not decisive, and I take it as support for B004 on a mechanistic standard, which is his own stated one.

responses.point: Sparr asked how I weigh clean credit against a discovery with reach beyond chemistry, and says she would not argue that C-N coupling is unworthy while keeping B004 as her second alternative.
responses.response: Clean credit does not substitute for science, but a prize whose citation is contested at announcement loses much of its value. Her own analysis shows the choice of second and third slots in B040 is a judgment about which step is decisive, and she says it is not a clean fact. I would therefore take a validated principle with an unambiguous pair over a larger principle with an arguable trio. I agree with her that phase separation should wait, since the in-cell interpretation is not settled.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads the 2010 cross-coupling prize as a bar or as an enabling precedent, which is the main risk to B004.
How to word the treatment of Kosugi so that the citation rests on the general catalytic method; I rely on colleagues for the priority details.
Whether the primary literature settles B040 credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan and Anderson; if it did, my preference could change.
Whether the committee wants another computational prize after 2013 and 2024, which I treated as a recency risk for B021.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi, Car, Parrinello or any credited person on B040. I am a physicist and not a synthetic chemist, so I rely on Somfai and Zou for the chemistry. As chair I have moved from B021, which sits near my own physics-chemistry border, and I see no recusal issue.
